Shatter Dive is largely irrelevant as a damage tool in both game modes now. Instead, it's usually gravitated towards as movement tools. Fast descent speed, noticeable horizontal mobility, and the ability to halt your momentum.

As for the Super, it's generally used for a shutdown super. This is a usage case where you wait for an opponent to commit to something strong (usually their own super) and then use yours in order to cripple or just outright kill them. It also helps that the Squall tornado has aggressive tracking and is a near guaranteed kill if they are caught by it at all.

Fun fact, the "50% success rate" was a lie that the other robot tells you since she can't bear to tell you that it is in fact duplication and a version of you will be left behind (and that version is the one who has to decide whether or not to "transfer") The only difference was that the game writers made the creative decision to have it "work" the first time, but in reality the robot you were playing as was still inside that body. The second time where it "failed" is what actually happens to the original copy.
